```{r load-packages}
library(tidyverse)
library(cluster)  # for silhouette()

options(bdat602.source_only = TRUE)
source("courses/bdat-602/_teacher/resources/datasets/simulate_bdat602_data.R")
# Use 5,000 rows — hclust needs O(n^2) memory
health_data <- simulate_bdat602(n = 5000, seed = 602)
```

## Task 1: Prepare the data

```{r task1-prepare}

  drop_na() |>
  NULL  # replace with scale()

dim(clust_data)
```

## Task 2: Fit hierarchical clustering (Ward linkage) and plot the dendrogram

```{r task2-hclust}
# TODO: compute the Euclidean distance matrix with dist()
D <- NULL  # dist(clust_data, method = "euclidean")

# TODO: fit hclust with method = "ward.D2"
hc <- NULL  # hclust(D, method = "ward.D2")

# TODO: plot the dendrogram
# Use labels = FALSE (too many to show), hang = -1 for a clean look
# Add a red dashed horizontal line at a height that gives ~4 clusters

plot(hc, labels = FALSE, hang = -1,
     main = "Ward.D2 Dendrogram — Insurance Policyholders")
```

## Task 3: Extract clusters and compare to k-means

```{r task3-cutree}
# TODO: use cutree() to extract 4 clusters from hc
clusters_hc <- NULL  # cutree(hc, k = 4)

# Print the size of each cluster
table(clusters_hc)
```

```{r task3-compare}
# For reference, run k-means with k = 4 on the same data
set.seed(602)
km4 <- kmeans(clust_data, centers = 4, nstart = 25)

# Compare cluster sizes
cat("Hierarchical cluster sizes:", table(clusters_hc), "\n")
cat("k-means cluster sizes:     ", km4$size, "\n")

# Are the cluster sizes similar? Which method produces more balanced clusters?
# Answer (as a comment):
```

## Task 4: Single linkage — chaining effect

```{r task4-single-linkage}
# TODO: re-fit hclust with method = "single"
hc_single <- NULL  # hclust(D, method = "single")

# TODO: plot the dendrogram for single linkage
plot(hc_single, labels = FALSE, hang = -1,
     main = "Single Linkage Dendrogram — Insurance Policyholders")
```

```{r task4-chaining}
# Extract 4 clusters from single linkage
clusters_single <- cutree(hc_single, k = 4)
table(clusters_single)
```
